evidence: Flowing through the heart of Hanoi, the Red River, known locally as Sông Hồng, has long served as the silent lifeblood nourishing the imperial land. This vast river, carrying heavy red alluvium, winds through alluvial flats, ancient bridges, and bustling neighborhoods, painting a unique picture that is distinctly Hanoi's. The ancient name "Nhị Hà" reflects its historical importance, while the modern name Sông Hồng originates from the crimson water color it takes on during the flood season, when the river brings layers of alluvium that have built up the entire Bắc Bộ Delta over thousands of years.
